name: Texas
agency: Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS), Driver License Division
permitAge: 15 (learner license, ages 15 to 17), after the classroom part of driver education, a vision exam and the knowledge exam (handbook p. 1)

teen.supervisedHours: 30 hours of behind-the-wheel practice, at least 10 at night, with a licensed driver 21 or older (DPS teen provisional page; not in the handbook)
teen.nightLimit: Provisional license under 18: no driving midnight to 5 a.m. unless for work, a school-related activity or a medical emergency (handbook p. 3)
teen.passengerLimit: Provisional license under 18: no more than one passenger under 21 who is not a family member (handbook p. 3)
teen.phone: Drivers under 18: no wireless communication device at all, hands-free included, except in an emergency (handbook p. 3). All drivers: no reading, writing or sending messages on a portable device while driving (handbook p. 54; Transp. Code 545.4251); no hand-held device in a school crossing zone (handbook p. 31; Transp. Code 545.425).

bac.under21: any detectable amount (zero tolerance, handbook p. 56)

notes: Checked 2026-10-09 against the Texas Driver Handbook DL-7, "Revised January 2026" (PDF dated 2026-01-28), English. Printed page = PDF page minus 6.
Learner license supervisor: licensed, at least 21, at least one year of driving experience, in the seat beside the driver (Transp. Code 521.222).

Move over / slow down (Transp. Code 545.157): vacate the lane closest to the stopped vehicle, or slow to 20 mph below the limit; 5 mph when the limit is 25 or less. Since Sept. 1, 2025 also covers animal control and parking enforcement vehicles (TxDOT).

School bus (Transp. Code 545.066): opposite-direction traffic need not stop only on separate roadways (intervening space or physical barrier); a center left-turn lane does not count. First offense fine $500 to $1,250.
Urban district prima facie limit 30 mph; 70 mph on numbered highways outside urban districts (Transp. Code 545.352); higher limits by order on some roads, not used in questions.
Knowledge exam pass mark 70 percent or better (handbook p. 7). Number of questions is not in the handbook or on DPS pages read; commercial sites say 30.

Test languages: 37 TAC 15.52 says written and oral tests are given in English and Spanish only (read via the Cornell LII copy; the official SOS rule site is a script-only app, and the handbook does not say). exam.languages left out for that reason.

Impact Texas Teen Drivers (ITTD) within 90 days before the driving test (DPS teen provisional page). Handbook p. 7 only says the Impact Texas Drivers course for your age group is required before the driving exam.
Spanish handbook DL-7S: the DPS forms page and https://www.dps.texas.gov/internetforms/Forms/DL-7S.pdf returned "Request Rejected" (bot filter) on 2026-10-09; not confirmed.

Handbook p. 23 states the move-over rule as: leave the lane next to the vehicle, or slow to 20 mph below a limit of 25 or more, or under 5 mph when the limit is below 25. Handbook p. 46 repeats it with tow trucks, utility and TxDOT vehicles.
